title: Spotify terminal player
brief: Control a Spotify Premium account from the terminal (Spotify Connect, remote playback), k9s/lazygit keyboard model, no modal editing. Main jobs: search any track and play it, browse albums, playlists and liked songs, manage the queue. Three directions for the main screen.

artboards.title: Full-screen list with queue drawer
artboards.tradeoff: One list owns the whole 180 columns, so titles, artist and album never truncate; the queue is a drawer you toggle with q. Costs you the always-visible queue and one keypress per view change.

artboards.title: Stack table
artboards.tradeoff: One maximised table per view with six columns and a one-row collection strip. Best scanability and sorting for large lists; you lose the persistent queue and need a key to see it.

artboards.title: Command first
artboards.tradeoff: The palette is the primary entry point: fastest path from thought to a specific track, and type-grouped fuzzy results. Weaker for browsing an album or a playlist by structure, and it is the least discoverable of the three.
